subject: Acme Analytics — confirmation of privacy & data integrity checks after KV cache anomaly
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.dev>
To: maya.rao@acme-analytics.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.dev, rishi_malhotra@redwood.dev
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: KV cache anomaly — initial customer notification and privacy check

Hi Maya,

I wanted to reach out directly about an incident we observed this morning affecting a subset of KV cache requests in the Redwood serving layer for your workspace (region: us-west-2). The issue caused intermittent failures and delayed cache refreshes between 08:30–09:05 PDT.

We prioritize data integrity and privacy—our initial triage focused on determining whether any customer data was lost or left our environment. Engineering has begun a full set of log and egress checks. At this stage we see no indication of data loss or external data transfers, but we are still completing corroborating queries across audit logs, S3 events, and network egress logs.

We’ll provide an evidence-backed confirmation (log excerpts and summary) by EOD today and a draft postmortem with technical details and mitigations within 48 hours. If you prefer a quick call to review the checks, I can arrange one this afternoon.

Apologies for the disruption — we know how disruptive any uncertainty around data integrity can be.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.dev
+1 (415) 555-0128

Attachments: (none in this message)
From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@acme-analytics.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.dev
Cc: security@acme-analytics.com, nick.patel@acme-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:33:41 -0700
Subject: Re: KV cache anomaly — initial customer notification and privacy check

Hannah — thanks for the heads up. Two quick asks: 1) Can you confirm the scope (which tenants/keys were impacted) and whether any PII or customer payloads were involved? 2) Please confirm whether any third-party services (e.g., external storage or telemetry) saw our data during this window.

We need to document this for our internal compliance and will escalate if there was any exposure. If you can share a concise evidence packet (log query results, egress scan summary, and the postmortem link) that would be ideal.

Maya Rao
Head of InfoSec, Acme Analytics
maya.rao@acme-analytics.com

On a related note, do you have an ETA for the root cause and mitigation timeline?
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.dev>
To: maya.rao@acme-analytics.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.dev, marissa_cole@redwood.dev
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 12:07:12 -0700
Subject: Re: KV cache anomaly — initial customer notification and privacy check

Hi Maya — I’m the SRE on the incident. Per your asks, here’s what we’ve completed and the short answers up front: scope = a small fraction of KV shard owners servicing ephemeral request routing for long-tail keys; impacted tenants identified by internal shard-id list (we included your workspace in the sample set for verification) — PII/payloads: no evidence of content corruption or deletion; third-party exposure: no outbound transfers observed.

Checks performed (summary):
- Audit log queries: scanned write/delete operations for the 08:00–10:00 PDT window across the tenant namespace (query id: audit-q-20260602-1). Results: zero delete operations and a normal rate of writes.
- KV integrity verification: ran checksum reconcilers across the affected shards vs. cold storage snapshots (run id: kv-check-20260602-7). All checksums matched.
- Network egress scan: correlated VPC flow logs and packet capture for candidate nodes; no anomalous external TCP sessions initiated to unknown endpoints during the window (scan id: egress-scan-20260602-2).
- Object store audit: checked S3 server access logs and last-modified events for objects tied to the affected caches — no unexpected GET/PUTs from external principals.
- KMS/HSM access logs: validated that there were no unusual key usage patterns during the incident window.

Attached are the raw CSV export of the audit query (kv_cache_audit_log_20260602.csv) and a related egress scan output (egress-check-scan-outputs.txt). We are packaging a concise evidence packet and the postmortem draft (postmortem-draft-acme-20260602.pdf) for your records.

Short, careful summary for your compliance team: after exhaustive log and artifact checks across storage, network, and key management layers, we found no evidence of data exfiltration, no object deletions, and checksums confirm cached data integrity. We will include the exact queries and verification commands in the final postmortem.

If your team would like to review the log queries or run additional checks against any specific object IDs you provide, we can prioritize that.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
SRE, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.dev

Attachments: kv_cache_audit_log_20260602.csv, egress-check-scan-outputs.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.dev>
To: maya.rao@acme-analytics.com
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.dev, rishi_malhotra@redwood.dev
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KV cache anomaly — initial customer notification and privacy check

Maya — following up with the confirmed post-incident materials. We’ve published the incident draft and supporting artifacts to a secure drive link and uploaded the ticket to our postmortem tracker: https://drive.redwood.com/postmortems/RI-9876-acme-kv-cache (link expires in 30 days). The draft contains: timeline, root cause analysis, how we verified data integrity (full queries listed), customer impact summary, and mitigations deployed (hotfix rolled at 09:10 PDT; throttling adjustments and a config guard added).

Next steps we propose:
- 1:1 review with your security team (we have availability tomorrow 10:00–11:30 PDT)
- Provide signed evidence bundle (CSV exports + audit log hashes) if you require chain-of-custody for compliance
- Add Acme as a tracked workspace for extended monitoring and a short retention of detailed debug logs for 30 days at our expense

Please let us know which option you prefer. Thanks again for patience; we’ll keep this at top priority.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.dev

Attachments: postmortem-draft-acme-20260602.pdf
